top.title: Ary Borges on Arthur Elias: “He works with us and understands players”
top.description: Ary Borges on Arthur Elias: “He works with us and understands players” Alongside her strong form at Angel City and her string of call-ups to the Brazilian national team, motherhood has brought a new chapter to Ary Borges’ journey. At a press conference on Thursday (26), the midfielder highlighted the support she received from head coach Arthur Elias and spoke about the importance of his understanding when he left her out of October’s international window so she could spend the first days of her newborn daughter Melanie’s life alongside her wife, Gabriela. “This is a very special time for me. Arthur is a very caring person who really values relationships, both individually and as a group. In this situation, he showed once again how much he stands by us and understands the players. Arthur watched me grow at Centro Olímpico, and now he has watched me become a mother,” she said. “Before the last squad announcement, he called me, asked about my family and was very honest with me. He said that my saying no at that moment (to joining the squad) was actually saying yes. As athletes, we give up so much, and he gave me peace of mind to enjoy a special moment with my family. He also reassured other players who want to become mothers but worry it could affect their careers,” she added. Ary Borges during a Brazilian women’s national team training session in Hiroshima, Japan Credit: Luciana Vermell/CBF Ary has known Arthur Elias since her days at Centro Olímpico, where she played between 2015 and 2016. As a youngster, she would talk with her teammates about the possibility of being a ball girl at matches involving the team he coached. Years later, he would become her coach with the Brazilian national team and her nemesis in matches between Corinthians and Palmeiras, as she played for Palmeiras from 2020 to 2022, during a period of Corinthians dominance. Among the players called up for this international window, Ary logged the most playing time for her club, Angel City in the United States. She made 28 appearances and played 2,688 minutes, figures that underline her consistent involvement throughout the season. Speaking about the challenges facing Brazil in Japan, the midfielder highlighted the importance of the friendlies against the hosts as part of their World Cup preparations. “We’re very happy to be here in Japan and experience a different culture. Our profession gives us that privilege. In football terms, Japan are opponents who present us with plenty of challenges. This is another opportunity for us to study, improve and work toward our main goal, which is getting closer and closer (the World Cup). These have all the makings of two very interesting games, and I hope that, just like last time, we come away with two wins,” she said. top.title: ‘I bought a book on how to have a boy-child’ – Makinde
top.description: By Angel Aniobi Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde has revealed that he bought a book and ovulation kits with his wife in their attempt to have a male child after welcoming two daughters. Makinde made this disclosure during an interview with media personality Chude Jideonwo, where he spoke about his family, fatherhood and the decision to have a third child. Recounting how they planned their family, the governor said he initially wanted just one child but reluctantly agreed to have two after his wife questioned why they should have only one. According to him, he was comfortable with having two daughters and did not consider the gender of his children important. “Gender doesn’t mean anything to me because I felt whether a girl or a boy, it’s all linked up to how you’re going to bring them up and how you set them up to impact their environment, and you can do it with any kid,” he said. Makinde, however, explained that cultural expectations and comments from his mother-in-law amplified his wife’s desire to have a male child. He said his mother-in-law told his wife that Yoruba men whose wives did not give birth to boys could seek to have a male child outside their marriages. “I’m a Yoruba man, but I think I am okay with the girls that God has blessed us with,” he recalled saying. The governor disclosed that it took more than five years for him to understand his wife’s desire to have a son, after which they agreed to explore ways of having a male child. He said he subsequently purchased a book on how to conceive a boy, which they both read and followed, alongside purchasing ovulation kits. “So, I said, okay, well, that’s fine. We have to go and buy a book on how to have a boy, and then we’ll read it and apply strictly,” he said. Makinde added that their efforts eventually resulted in the birth of their son, who became their third child. “That was it. That was what produced the boy, and I was finally left off the hook,” he said. Vanguard News The post ‘I bought a book on how to have a boy-child’ – Makinde appeared first on Vanguard News .

top.title: Rams grind out 26-13 win over Packers on Thanksgiving Eve
top.description: Nov 25, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love (10) throws a pass during the first quarter against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images INGLEWOOD, Calif. — Blake Corum turned 26 on Wednesday and celebrated with a career-best performance, carrying the ball 32 times for 184 yards and a touchdown as the Los Angeles Rams controlled the clock and the trenches in a 26-13 victory over the Green Bay Packers . It was the NFL’s first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game, and the Rams used it to extend their winning streak to five and improve to 7-4. Corum’s 32 carries were the most by a Rams running back in Sean McVay’s decade in charge. He scored for the seventh straight game, and Kyren Williams added a touchdown and 46 yards on 12 carries as Los Angeles finished with 241 rushing yards. Brandon McManus contributed four field goals. Matthew Stafford needed only 16 completions on 23 attempts for 140 yards (and one interception) as the Rams leaned on the ground game against an injury-thinned receiving corps. The teams were tied 13-13 at halftime. Green Bay had clawed back from an early deficit behind a Christian Watson touchdown catch, but the second half belonged entirely to the Rams. Los Angeles outscored the Packers 13-0 after the break, held Green Bay to just 55 rushing yards, and dominated time of possession (40:40 to 19:20). Jordan Love finished 17-of-29 for 198 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions. The Packers fell to 6-5 after their second straight loss. The night was not without controversy. Rams safety Kamren Kinchens was ejected for a helmet-to-helmet hit on Watson late in the second quarter; Watson was ruled out with a concussion after catching four passes for 65 yards and the score. Micah Parsons, returning from a torn ACL, recorded a sack for Green Bay, but the Packers could not generate consistent offense once the Rams established their rushing rhythm. The result carries clear playoff weight. Both teams entered at 6-4 in a crowded NFC wild-card race; the head-to-head win and the possession edge now give the Rams a clearer path. Los Angeles hosts the Kansas City Chiefs next, while Green Bay travels to face the New Orleans Saints.

top.title: Jackson’s Future In Miami Looks Grim Despite Sunday’s Start
top.description: Credit: David Santiago-Imagn Images The Miami Dolphins are staring down a massive decision at right tackle, and the writing is on the wall for Austin Jackson. Yahoo Sports NFL reports that Jackson is in the last year of his contract while the coaching staff actively weighs a change at the position. This is a bad week and likely the end of his time in South Florida. Proctor Stays Put for Now While some reports suggest Proctor is the heir apparent to the right tackle spot, Head Coach Jeff Hafley shut down that talk before practice on Wednesday. Per Sports Illustrated , Proctor will not be moving to right tackle this week and might not make the switch at all this season. The team is sticking with Jackson for now, barring an injury that forces him out of the upcoming game against the New York Jets. Hafley did not say exactly what is wrong with Jackson, only that the player would be limited in practice on Wednesday. The coach added that Jackson is expected to line up at his spot at right tackle when the Jets visit Hard Rock Stadium on Sunday. This leaves the Dolphins in a weird spot, relying on a player who has struggled all season while holding a rookie guard back from his natural progression. Looking Beyond the Current Roster The front office is clearly weighing long-term options while trying to win the next game. If the team moves on from Jackson, they have seen other players step up elsewhere in the league. Chukwuebuka Godrick started three games for the Kansas City Chiefs last season, and Caedan Wallace has two career starts on his resume with the New England Patriots. Wallace started one game at left tackle and the other as a sixth offensive lineman, showing he can handle different roles. The Dolphins also have a pass rush to worry about on the other side of the ball. Rookie pass rusher David Bailey is the second overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft and is tied for third in the NFL with 9.5 sacks. During their first meeting in Week 7, the Dolphins limited him to four tackles and half a sack over 61 snaps, with Bailey recording those statistics. The team faces the Jets this Sunday at 1 p.m.

top.title: Detroit Tigers Sign Two Familiar Faces
top.description: The Detroit Tigers are bringing back a pair of familiar faces just one week after parting ways with them. According to Tigers beat writer Evan Woodbery of MLive, the organization has signed infielder Trey Sweeney and left-handed pitcher Jake Miller to minor-league contracts after non-tendering both players last week. The moves allow Tigers president of baseball operations Scott Harris to retain both players without committing spots on the 40-man roster. It is a strategy that has become somewhat familiar during Harris’ tenure in Detroit. Sep 23, 2025; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Detroit Tigers shortstop Trey Sweeney (27) throws to first in the third inning against the Cleveland Guardians at Progressive Field. Mandatory Credit: David Richard-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Detroit Tigers Re-Sign Trey Sweeney and Jake Miller Both signings are confirmed on the Tigers’ official transaction page , which lists the moves as taking place on November 25. Sweeney and Miller had been among the four players Detroit designated for assignment on November 17 before officially becoming free agents. Sweeney, 26, provides the Tigers with additional infield depth as he works to reestablish himself following an injury-plagued 2026 campaign. Although there is no guarantee he will return to the major league roster, keeping him in the organization makes sense for Detroit. Meanwhile, Miller, 25, is an intriguing left-handed pitching prospect who missed a significant portion of last season with a hip injury. According to NBC Sports , Miller posted a 0.77 ERA and struck out 24 batters across 23 1/3 minor-league innings in 2026. Scott Harris Continues Familiar Roster-Building Strategy As Woodbery pointed out Thursday morning, Harris has had considerable success convincing players who have been non-tendered to return to the Tigers on minor-league contracts. The strategy allows Detroit to retain organizational depth while maintaining flexibility on its 40-man roster. Sweeney and Miller were two of the three players the Tigers non-tendered ahead of last week’s deadline , with outfielder Matt Vierling being the other. Whether Vierling could eventually return to the organization remains to be seen. Neither signing is going to generate the excitement of a major free-agent acquisition, but these are the types of low-risk moves that can pay dividends over the course of a 162-game season. In Miller’s case, particularly, there is enough upside to make bringing him back a worthwhile investment.

top.title: WNBA’s 2027 Cap Math Leaves Little Room For Error For Dream
top.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images The WNBA salary cap rules for 2027 create a harsh reality for teams trying to build a winner. The Atlanta Dream faces a math problem that leaves almost no room for maneuvering. According to Sports Illustrated , the league cap can rise by no more than 13% to $7.91 million. This small jump does not help teams that already have limited space. The Dream must sign three new players just to fill their roster. Each of these new signings costs at least $280,800. That adds up fast and eats into the money available for star talent. The Minimum Salary Trap Every team must keep 12 players on the roster during the season. This rule forces franchises to spend money they might prefer to save. Per Sports Illustrated, the lowest full-season minimum salary for a player with no experience is $280,800 in 2027. The Dream already has nine players under contract totaling about $6.18 million. To reach the required 12 players, the team needs to spend an extra $842,400 on new signings. This mandatory spending pushes their total obligations to $7.02 million. The math leaves the team with very little flexibility to sign big free agents. Where the Money Goes The gap between the total cap and what a team can actually spend is now wider than ever. The Atlanta Dream will have to spend $7.02 million just to meet basic roster requirements. This leaves them with about $886,000 to spend freely on top-tier talent. That amount is tiny compared to the cost of a supermax deal. A supermax salary is 20% of the cap for a given year, which would be roughly $1.58 million. Only the current club or, in the event of free agency, the former club can sign an eligible player to a supermax. This restriction makes it hard for other teams to poach stars from the Dream without paying a premium. Spending Limits and Roster Rules A team’s payroll cannot surpass the salary cap at any moment unless it applies a hardship, emergency hardship, pregnancy/childbirth, or season-ending injury exception. For any specific year, the standard maximum salary equals 17% of the salary cap. These tight limits mean teams cannot simply throw money at every problem. They must plan carefully or risk breaking the rules. The Dream’s situation shows how the new rules squeeze out spending power. With only $886,000 left for free spending, the team has very few options to improve the roster beyond the minimums. The Dream, in its present form, must spend $7.02 million, which leaves approximately $886,000 available for unrestricted spending above minimum salaries.

top.title: Why do the Lions and Cowboys always play on Thanksgiving?
top.description: Detroit Lions fans dress for Thanksgiving game against the Chicago Bears, Thursday, Nov. 28, 2019 at Ford Field. Detroit Lions fans | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co There are three NFL games today. The Lions host the Bears, the Cowboys host the Eagles, and the Bills host the Chiefs. The teams playing the night game change annually, but you might notice that the Lions always host the first game of the day, and the Cowboys always host the second game. How did that come to be? The Lions played their first Thanksgiving game in 1934. It was their first season in Detroit. They had previously been located in Portsmouth, Ohio, where they were known as the Portsmouth Spartans. A radio executive named George Richards bought the franchise and moved it to Detroit. The Lions were having difficulty gaining any sort of popularity in their new home city. Richards came up with the idea of scheduling their team’s big game against the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving. The Lions were 10-1 at the time, and the Bears were 11-0. This was before the days when the league dictated the schedule to its teams. The teams themselves could schedule the times of their games. Richards used his connections in the radio business to get the game broadcast nationally. Even thought Detroit lost, it was a huge success. The Lions sold the game out, and they have played on Thanksgiving ever since with the exception of World War II years despite some calls for them to lose the game during the dismal Matt Millen Era. Thanksgiving gained a second traditional team in 1951. For the next thirteen years, the Green Bay Packers traveled to Detroit to play the Lions on Thanksgiving. Vince Lombardi ended the arrangement. Lombardi cited the end of an agreement that paid the Packers $10,000 extra for playing the game, the difficulties of playing games on a short week every year, and having to face a rival in front of an electric crowd on the road every season. Of course since the teams are in the same division, the Packers remain a frequent Thanksgiving opponent for Detroit. So how about the Cowboys? In the mid-1960’s the NFL was looking to add a second Thanksgiving game. It was not entirely clear it would work outside Detroit, where Thanksgiving NFL was already a tradition. The Dallas Cowboys were a six year old team with no history of winning. General manager Tex Schramm was a visionary. (He was a driving force behind other innovations like instant replay, the flags on goal posts, the NFL-AFL merger, and too many others to name). He jumped at the opportunity. The Cowboys hosted their first Thanksgiving game in 1966. They kept the game annually until the 1970’s when the league hatched a plan to alternate between the Cowboys and the then St. Louis Cardinals . The Cowboys were to host the second game in even years and the Cardinals in odd years. The Cardinals only hosted two home Thanksgiving games, however, which took place in 1975 and in 1977. top.title: Christian Pulisic, Antoine Griezmann and Emma Hayes’ USWNT: Why American soccer fans have plenty to celebrate this Thanksgiving
top.description: Thanksgiving 2026 GFX - GOAL GOAL breaks down what you should be thankful for during this holiday season. It's Thanksgiving, and we all know what that means. Turkey, gravy, mashed potatoes, stuffing - all on the menu. There's plenty to be thankful for, but that doesn't just extend to food; it extends to soccer, too. Obviously, there are more important things in life to give thanks for at this time of year, but it is also worth acknowledging the sport's role in everyday life. For some, it's an obsession. For others, it's a distraction. But, if you're reading this story, it's safe to assume that you're glad that soccer is a part of your life in some way. So, with that in mind, let's sit down, put down the fork for a moment and give thanks for all of the good things about American soccer and, just as crucially, all of the things worth being excited for on the horizon, too. The 2026 World Cup Spain helped make the 2026 World Cup a summer to remember as fans from across the globe came together in America. Yeah, it's over now, but what a ride it was! For one summer, soccer came stateside and, for one summer, America was at the forefront of the beautiful game. The scenes were unforgettable: the games, the pageantry, the fans sweeping through cities. Scotland in Boston, Algeria in Kansas, Norway's Viking Row taking over Times Square - it was a wonderfully unifying experience, one that saw fans from all over the world experience American hospitality. It also saw Americans experience a taste of the unknown as they learned about those who had arrived for a summer of fun. From a USMNT perspective, yes, the ending was rough, but the road there was full of highs. The wins over Paraguay and Australia were unlike anything the world had seen from an American team. The Turkey game, despite the defeat, had several feel-good moments. Even the Bosnia and Herzegovina game that began the downturn was full of both grit and talent that inspired onlookers all over the world. So, before we turn the page, a toast to the 2026 World Cup and a thank you to all who made it special. Copa America, Olympics and Women's World Cup on the way More tournaments will soon be arriving on American shores. And, if you liked the World Cup experience, get ready for more, because there's more coming. Just this week, it was confirmed that both the 2031 Women's World Cup and 2028 Copa America will be coming to the U.S., bringing two more major tournaments stateside. You can also tack on the 2028 Olympics, too, giving fans another huge competition worth being excited to watch for both the men's and women's sides. For years, many looked at the 2026 World Cup as the pinnacle, the end of one era of American soccer. It turns out that wasn't the case; it was a huge, huge part, yes, but it was merely the latest step on a journey that, thankfully, includes plenty of big games stateside. top.title: Tiger Woods is making another comeback. Can his battered body hold up this time? | Opinion
top.description: How the other half lives, huh? I was reading one of those “day in the life” articles over the weekend, and it featured some guy called Scotch McClure, who is a big shot in the multibillion-dollar world of longevity tech, although his name does sound like something you’d find on the drink specials at my local bar. Anyway, ahead of another busy day at work, Scotch gets up at the crack of dawn every morning to meditate. “It’s how I align my chakras and bring my body and mind into coherence,” declared Scotch. I’m not sure what, or where, my own chakras are. My wife suggested they might be in that junk drawer with the Allen wrenches and obsolete phone chargers. But if I do stumble upon them, I can guarantee the damn things won’t be aligned. In fact, forget about aligning my chakras. I have enough trouble with the alignment in the setup of my golf swing, as the whole process, and inevitably disastrous results, drags my body and mind into complete incoherence. On the subject of the swing, I saw another article about research conducted by university psychologists that found golfers who think too much about technique can actually hurt their game. If it’s any help to the researchers, I’d like to add that the process of swinging a club at a ball is considerably easier when you don’t have any technique worth thinking about in the first place. I should be a psychologist, huh? More: What can we expect from Tiger Woods at the Hero? A review of his returns after long layoffs Next week, meanwhile, we’ll all get to see Tiger Woods swinging a club again for the first time in ages. You probably heard the news the other day that Tiger is set to make comeback No. 146, or something like that, in the 20-man, no-cut Hero World Challenge in the Bahamas. Now, I know Woods used to dabble in a bit of meditation, but since his last competitive appearance in the 2024 Open at Royal Troon, there have been a few hits to the coherence of both body and mind. Those chakras have been all over the place. Three more surgeries, two on his back and one on his Achilles, added to the wear and tear on a body that creaks like an abandoned ship, while yet another car accident, a subsequent DUI charge and a stint in an inpatient rehab facility in Switzerland provided more dispiriting twists to the turbulent Tiger tale. But after all the trials and tribulations, it looks like he’ll be back. Again. Will it be another short-lived exercise in futility? Who knows, but rightly or wrongly, a good chunk of the golf world will no doubt be captivated by this latest, tentative return to competition. top.title: 'Don't you change': Bill Cowher praises Dan Campbell
top.description: Credit: CBS Sports Dan Campbell has made Thanksgiving football much more enjoyable for millions of people across the country by making the Detroit Lions more competitive in recent years. The way he has led his team has won over even more fans along the way , including former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach and NFL Today analyst Bill Cowher. When you think of Dan Campbell, you think of him as the ultimate football tough guy. But he hasn’t been afraid to wear his heart on his sleeve . And when Cowher gave him his flowers for an interview for The NFL Today on CBS ahead of the Lions hosting the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving Day, he couldn’t help but get emotional. This is awesome Dan Campbell got emotional when @CowherCBS gave him his flowers #nflt https://t.co/Zg2IFfrBwv — NFL on CBS (@NFLonCBS) November 25, 2026 “I’d love to give thanks to you and what you represent, the journey that you’ve taken from a player to an assistant coach to climbing that ladder and landing here in Detroit; you embody what this place is all about. Yeah, you speak about resiliency, that’s Dan Campbell. You speak about grit, that’s Dan Campbell. You think about passion, that’s Dan Campbell,” Cowher said. “Thank you for being you. You’re authentic, man. And I don’t want you to ever change. Not only in the National Football League but this city, we need more people like Dan Campbell to continue to be a part of this society. As you keep your strive and pursuit for excellence is what’s made this country great, and you represent every element of that. Thank you for being you, and don’t you dare change. You bite the knees off on your way to getting that championship. Don’t you change, man.” After seeing Bill Cowher coach up Dan Campbell like that, with the emotion and intensity and pride on his own face, it’s almost a shame that the former Steelers coach never did return to the sidelines after his retirement after the 2006 season. That was an inspiring, powerful message. If you could ever get the two of them in the same locker room, players would run through any brick wall they could. top.title: Driver Arrested Over Crash, Inferno That Killed 31 In Egypt
top.description: Egyptian prosecutors announced on Thursday the arrest of a man accused of causing a massive fire that erupted when a fuel tanker overturned on a packed highway in Cairo, killing 31 people . The prosecution said the man had “admitted” to speeding when his car collided with the tanker, “causing the steering wheel to slip from his hands and his car to veer off course”. When the car hit the truck, one of its tyres exploded, causing it to overturn, the prosecution said. The fire erupted as a result of a petrol leak, it added. This video grab taken from UGC images posted on social media on November 25, 2026, shows flames engulfing the area during a fire in the Al-Waraq neighbourhood of Imbaba district, Giza Governorate. Photo by – / VARIOUS SOURCES / AFP Footage from the scene showed a huge fireball and thick black smoke rising above the densely populated capital’s Al-Waraq neighbourhood as motorists on the ring road sounded their horns and struggled to get away. The prosecution said an investigation is underway to determine the driver’s criminal liability. The health ministry put the final toll at 31 dead and 21 wounded. More than 20 million people live in Greater Cairo, a sprawling and dense metropolis. With its informal residential areas and often dilapidated infrastructure, Egypt has suffered several deadly fires in recent years. Car crashes are common and often blamed on reckless driving, poor maintenance, and uneven law enforcement, with traffic laws also being widely flouted. Not long after, Jeff Passan reported that they had also signed LHP Patrick Sandoval to a three-year $42 million dollar deal. Look for more on those signings in the coming days. nigeria.title: ‘I bought a book on how to have a boy-child’ – Makinde
nigeria.description: By Angel Aniobi Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde has revealed that he bought a book and ovulation kits with his wife in their attempt to have a male child after welcoming two daughters. Makinde made this disclosure during an interview with media personality Chude Jideonwo, where he spoke about his family, fatherhood and the decision to have a third child. Recounting how they planned their family, the governor said he initially wanted just one child but reluctantly agreed to have two after his wife questioned why they should have only one. According to him, he was comfortable with having two daughters and did not consider the gender of his children important. “Gender doesn’t mean anything to me because I felt whether a girl or a boy, it’s all linked up to how you’re going to bring them up and how you set them up to impact their environment, and you can do it with any kid,” he said. Makinde, however, explained that cultural expectations and comments from his mother-in-law amplified his wife’s desire to have a male child. He said his mother-in-law told his wife that Yoruba men whose wives did not give birth to boys could seek to have a male child outside their marriages. “I’m a Yoruba man, but I think I am okay with the girls that God has blessed us with,” he recalled saying. The governor disclosed that it took more than five years for him to understand his wife’s desire to have a son, after which they agreed to explore ways of having a male child. He said he subsequently purchased a book on how to conceive a boy, which they both read and followed, alongside purchasing ovulation kits. “So, I said, okay, well, that’s fine. We have to go and buy a book on how to have a boy, and then we’ll read it and apply strictly,” he said. Makinde added that their efforts eventually resulted in the birth of their son, who became their third child. “That was it. That was what produced the boy, and I was finally left off the hook,” he said. Vanguard News The post ‘I bought a book on how to have a boy-child’ – Makinde appeared first on Vanguard News .

Comedian Bovi, who was among the audience, asked Teni why the sisters had never collaborated on a song, prompting her to explain that their conversations rarely revolve around music. According to her, whenever they meet or speak, they spend most of their time chatting and discussing other matters rather than working on music. “We are just two crazy girls. We will just be doing amebo and gisting all the time, forgetting to make music,” she said. She added that music hardly comes up whenever they speak, but suggested that fans could finally get the long-awaited collaboration in 2027. “I kid you not, every time Nini and I talk, we never talk about music. I know it’s bad. We are going to give you guys come 2027,” Teni said. The singer’s comments have renewed anticipation among fans for a joint project from the sisters, whose careers have developed independently within the Nigerian music industry. Teni, whose full name is Teniola Apata, gained prominence with songs such as Uyo Meyo and Case , while Niniola, born Niniola Apata, established herself with popular tracks including Maradona and Bana . Both singers have earned recognition for their distinct musical styles, with Teni known for her playful delivery and Niniola celebrated for her blend of Afro-house and other contemporary African sounds. Although they have not released a joint song, Teni’s latest remarks suggest that a collaboration could be on the way in 2027. The woman reportedly went into labour and delivered her baby in the early hours of Thursday after being rushed to a hospital following the incident. The incident occurred at No. 1 Anyeji Omenwa Street, Obosi, where the officials allegedly padlocked the main entrance to the compound and sealed the building with red tape. The sealing reportedly left the landlady, Prophetess Ukamaka Lauretta Okafor, tenants and other occupants of the three-storey building, comprising 11 flats and rooms in the boys’ quarters, unable to gain access to their homes. The landlady, who protested the action, accused APLUC officials of refusing to issue her a receipt for the N120,000 she allegedly paid to the agency in February, while demanding additional payments. Addressing journalists on Thursday, Okafor said she was not indebted to the agency, insisting that the officials had failed to provide evidence of the full payment she made. She alleged that although N120,000 was deducted from her account through the officials’ Point of Sale (POS) machine, she was issued a receipt for only N90,000. According to her, the officials promised to provide a receipt for the outstanding N30,000 at their office but failed to do so despite her repeated visits. She said she was subsequently informed that the N120,000 payment covered her 2024 liability, while further payments were required for 2025 and 2026. Okafor said she expressed willingness to settle the outstanding payments but insisted that she must first receive evidence of the previous payment. She alleged that the officials refused to issue receipts or a covering note for subsequent payments, instead asking her to pay cash or surrender her ATM card for transactions through their POS machine. She said: “As I am speaking with you now, the N120,000 I paid in February this year, they have not given me the receipt. “I now told them that I will not continue to pay money that won’t be receipted or any evidence of payment given to me. The Controller General of the Federal Fire Service FFS, Samuel Adeyemi Olumode, gave the advisory on Thursday while flagging off the 2026 Harmattan Fire Safety Campaign. The campaign will run through February 2027. He spoke via a virtual fire chat on “The Roles and Responsibilities of Stakeholders in Building a Fire Safety-Resilient Community.” “The Harmattan period comes with dry and dusty weather conditions, low humidity and dry vegetation, all of which can contribute to the rapid spread of fire. “Activities involving cooking, electrical appliances, generators, gas cylinders, fuel storage and open burning require greater caution during this period”, he said. One of our personnel sustained a head injury and required medical attention. “Let me state clearly that attacks on firefighters will not be tolerated,” Olumode declared, adding that the suspected perpetrators had been apprehended. “Let me assure Nigerians that this matter will not be treated lightly. nigeria.title: WhatsApp to allow users schedule messages – here’s how you can
nigeria.description: WhatsApp has introduced a scheduled messaging feature that allows users to compose messages in advance and choose when they should be delivered, addressing one of the most requested additions to the messaging platform. The feature will enable users to schedule messages between 10 minutes and 14 days ahead in both individual and group chats. Announcing the update, WhatsApp said the feature would allow users to write messages when they think of them and have them delivered at a more appropriate time. “That’s why we’re introducing scheduled messages – one of our most requested features. You can write a message when you think of it and send it anywhere from 10 minutes to 14 days later, in both your 1:1 and group chats,” the company said. According to WhatsApp, scheduled messages will appear in recipients’ chats like ordinary messages, without any indication that they were composed and scheduled earlier. Users will also be able to view all their scheduled messages and delete them before delivery if they change their minds. How to schedule messages on WhatsApp To schedule a message on WhatsApp, users can follow these steps: Open WhatsApp and select an individual or group chat. Type the message they want to send. Press and hold the send button. Select the preferred date and time for the message to be delivered. Confirm the schedule. The message will then be delivered automatically at the selected time. WhatsApp said scheduled messages would still be delivered even if the sender’s phone was switched off or ran out of battery. The feature will support text messages, photographs and videos, giving users the option to plan different types of communication ahead of time. The company also assured users that scheduled messages would retain WhatsApp’s end-to-end encryption, meaning only the sender and intended recipients would be able to read them. “Even if your phone is off or out of battery, your scheduled message will still show up at the time you chose, and it remains end-to-end encrypted like all your personal messages, so no one else can read it, not even us,” WhatsApp said. The scheduled messaging feature is rolling out globally over the coming weeks, although the company did not specify when it would become available to all users. WhatsApp said the update was another way for users to stay connected with important people by ensuring their messages arrive at exactly the right time. nigeria.description: By Godwin Oritse Nigeria’s expanding trade activities are increasingly highlighting the strategic importance of the maritime sector, with cargo volumes handled across the nation’s seaports recording significant growth amid rising merchandise trade. The Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) disclosed that cargo throughput across Nigerian ports rose by 24.8 per cent, from 103.6 million metric tonnes in 2024 to 129.3 million metric tonnes in 2025, indicating increased port utilisation and growing cargo-handling activities. The growth momentum extended into the first half of 2026, as cargo throughput increased by 12.2 per cent to 68.2 million metric tonnes, compared with 60.8 million metric tonnes recorded in the corresponding period of 2025. The development comes against the backdrop of Nigeria’s merchandise trade rising to ₦41.4 trillion in the second quarter of 2026, further highlighting the critical role of ports in facilitating international trade, cargo movement and broader economic activities. He said Nigeria’s merchandise trade value of ₦41.4 trillion in the second quarter of 2026, representing a 5.6 per cent increase over the corresponding period of 2025, demonstrated the scale of economic activity linked to the movement of cargo through the country’s ports. According to him, port efficiency has far-reaching implications for manufacturers, exporters, importers, consumers and investors, as delays and operational bottlenecks ultimately increase the cost of doing business and affect the prices of goods. Onyemekara said the country’s ports received 2,300 ships in the first half of 2026, compared with 2,152 vessels in the same period of 2025, while outward cargo accounted for 41.9 per cent of total throughput in the second quarter, indicating improved export activity. nigeria.title: Plateau Attack: Death toll rises to 19
nigeria.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — The death toll from an attack on Tafi-Gana (Cando Zrreci), a community in Jebbu Miango, Bassa Local Government Area of Plateau State, has risen to 19 following the death of three persons who were rushed to hospital after the incident. The attack reportedly occurred on Wednesday night, November 25, and continued into the early hours of Thursday, November 26, 2026, throwing the community into confusion, fear and panic. A resident of the community, Moses Monday, who confirmed the casualty figure on Thursday, said 16 bodies were recovered at the scene, while three other victims died after being taken to hospital. Monday said: “This is evil. I can confirm that 16 bodies have so far been recovered at the spot, with an additional three who died after they were taken to the hospital. These evil men will not rest.” Another resident, Nuhu Fidelis, who also confirmed the attack, described it as another assault on a neighbouring community in Jebbu Miango. Fidelis said: “Yes, in the early morning of today, Thursday. Last night, November 25, 2026, a Christian neighbouring village, Tafi-Gana (Cando Zrreci), in Jebbu Miango, Bassa LGA, Plateau State, was attacked again. Many innocent people lost their lives.” He condemned the killings and called on the government and security agencies to take urgent measures to protect residents. Another resident, Paul Nehemiah, who said he lost a close relative in the attack, described the killings as wicked and unprovoked, adding that residents had been living in fear following repeated attacks. Nehemiah said: “We are tired of burying our people. These are farmers, women and children who did nothing to anyone. How long will this continue? We are calling on the government to rise up and save us.” Rita Joseph, whose family fled the village during the attack, said community members could no longer sleep peacefully because of persistent security threats. She said: “We ran into the bush with our children.” The residents appealed to the Plateau State Government, the Federal Government and security agencies to deploy more personnel to Miango and surrounding communities to prevent further attacks. They also urged the authorities to take decisive action to bring the perpetrators to justice and restore confidence among residents. nigeria.title: FIFA confirms cyberattack, says hackers stole personal, business data
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye FIFA has confirmed a criminal cyberattack that exposed a limited amount of personal and business information, while files linked to its abandoned World Cup stake-sale plan were not accessed. According to Reuters, a person with direct knowledge of the incident said less than 0.1 per cent of FIFA’s total data was affected and no files from the FIFA Forward Enterprise project were accessed. “FIFA can confirm that it has been the victim of a criminal cyberattack resulting in unauthorised access to a limited set of personal and business information,” a FIFA spokesperson told Reuters. The football governing body condemned the unlawful acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data, calling it “a serious and unacceptable violation of privacy”. FIFA did not disclose when the attack took place, how many people or organisations were affected, or what business information was accessed. It also did not say whether any data had appeared online or where it may have been published. FIFA scrapped plans in July to sell private investors a stake in a new unit that would manage its events, including the World Cup. nigeria.title: Meet Nigeria’s Damilola Bolarinde, crowned Miss International Africa 2026
nigeria.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nigerian beauty queen Damilola Bolarinde has been crowned Miss International Africa 2026 after representing the country at the 64th edition of the Miss International pageant in Tokyo, Japan. The continental title was announced on Thursday, November 26, a day after the grand finale held on November 25, which featured 73 contestants from different countries. Bolarinde, popularly known as Queen Dammy, secured a place among the Top 20 contestants but did not advance to the Top 10. Her performance at the competition earned her the Miss International Africa title. The achievement adds to her growing profile in the Nigerian beauty pageant industry, having represented Lagos State at the 2025 Miss Universe Nigeria competition, where she emerged first runner-up behind Anambra State representative, Onyinyechi Basil. In April 2026, Bolarinde won the Face of Hope pageant, earning the right to represent Nigeria at the Miss International competition as Miss International Nigeria 2026. She defeated contestants representing Anambra and Rivers states, who finished as first and second runners-up, respectively, at the event held on April 19 at the Eko Convention Centre in Lagos. Meanwhile, Elizaveta Kuznetsova of Moldova won the overall Miss International 2026 crown, becoming the first contestant from her country to claim the title. Brittany Feeney of the United Kingdom finished as first runner-up, while Laura Glozarová of the Czech Republic came third. Victoria Kosasieputri of Indonesia and Khánh Như Lê of Vietnam completed the Top Five, finishing fourth and fifth, respectively. Bolarinde’s continental recognition marks another milestone in her pageant career and adds Nigeria to the list of countries represented among the award recipients at the international competition. nigeria.title: Opposition coalition confirms Monday summit, to adopt 3 key documents
nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Coalition for Democracy has confirmed that the Second Summit of Nigeria’s opposition political parties will hold on Monday in Abuja, with participating parties expected to adopt three foundational documents. The coalition is a multiparty platform pioneered by the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) and Social Democratic Party (SDP). In a statement signed by Salihu Moh. Lukman on behalf of the coalition parties, it said the decision was reached on Wednesday night at the seventh meeting of its Central Leadership Committee. The statement said the leaders reached the decision “following extensive deliberations on the state of the nation, the prevailing political environment and the earlier resolution to suspend campaign activities on day of the Summit”. The leaders, however, made it clear that the suspension does not end inter-party engagement. “The leaders agreed that the suspension of campaign activities does not preclude the continuation of consultations and engagements among opposition political parties on matters of common interest, including electoral integrity, democratic participation and institutional reform,” the statement said. The documents to be considered and adopted are the National Covenant for Democratic Renewal, the Framework for Opposition Unity and the National Reform Programme. They were developed by working groups made up of representatives of the constituent parties after the inaugural summit of August 31, 2026. According to the statement, “the documents set out proposed mechanisms for inter-party cooperation and a framework for addressing national governance challenges.” The coalition leaders also reaffirmed their commitment “to working collectively to safeguard the integrity of the electoral process and protect the sanctity of the ballot across the country”. The coalition invited other opposition political parties to participate in the summit and “contribute to the ongoing consultations”. Three personalities will address the summit on the theme, “The Doctrine of a Necessary Democratic Opposition”. They are the Alaago of Kajola Alago, Ileshan, HRH Oba Oladipo Olaitan; Prof. Ango Abdullahi; and Chief S. N. Okeke. The statement said the summit is expected to bring together “national leaders of opposition political parties, elected representatives, former public officeholders, civil society leaders, representatives of the media, and observers from foreign diplomatic missions in Nigeria”. entertainment.title: As Nigeria Rethinks Teacher Education, Tunji Olowolafe Makes a Case for Better-Prepared Educators
entertainment.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. This includes recognising the College’s first-class degree graduates and NCE distinction holders, alongside the overall best NCE and degree graduates. Lecturers, selected based on student ratings, will also be honoured for their teaching contributions. The initiative builds on the Foundation’s existing investment in education, including Project Digi-Teach at Ekiti State University and GOMTECH in Are-Ekiti. For Dr. Olowolafe, the commitment to educators is also deeply personal. His mother was a teacher, his elder sister taught for years at Baptist Academy, Lagos, and his late wife, Gbemisola Olowolafe, was a lifelong educator. entertainment.title: Alero Ebigbeyi: Making a Case for Quality, Affordable Fashion with HÉYCH

In fashion, the conversation often begins with style, but it rarely ends there. Quality, affordability, accessibility and the story behind what we wear are increasingly becoming part of how consumers make their choices. For Alero Ebigbeyi, these are not just considerations; they are the principles shaping her latest venture, HÉYCH. The Nigerian fashion and clothing brand officially opened its retail store on November 10, bringing together fashion enthusiasts, media executives, influencers, friends and industry personalities for an introduction to the brand and its collections. Guests explored the space, examined the clothing and made purchases. Yet, amid the excitement of the launch, two observations kept coming up: the quality of the pieces and their affordability. With over 30 years of experience in this industry, I understand the importance of quality, production standards and delivering value to customers,” she says. Rethinking How Fashion Is Produced That understanding is reflected in one of the brand’s most significant decisions: its investment in local manufacturing. Behind HÉYCH’s retail offering is a manufacturing facility in Lagos, a strategic investment that gives the brand greater control over production while creating the capacity to fulfil orders in large quantities. For Ebigbeyi, local production is as much about business efficiency as it is about building something sustainable within Nigeria. entertainment.title: Nollywood Legend Pete Edochie Passes Away at 79
entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). A B or a C in his Cambridge A-levels felt like a possibility he wasn’t ready to entertain, so he didn’t write the exams. A few years later, at 23, he has graduated from the University of Ibadan with a B.Sc. in Statistics, First-Class Honours and a CGPA of 3.65/4.0. Somewhere along the way, he decided that fear was no longer going to make his decisions for him. When Williams got into UI, he had a rather ambitious plan: become the Best Graduating Student in his faculty. Getting there would require more than good intentions. There were 5:30am wake-ups, difficult Statistics courses, friends who became unofficial tutors, a ChatGPT Pro subscription in 300 level, job offers he turned down and one Demography exam that kept him awake for 36 hours. University, as it turns out, came with quite a few plot twists. In this interview with BellaNaija, Williams takes us through the habits, people and decisions that shaped his academic journey. I knew becoming the overall Best Graduating Student in the university would require an extraordinary amount of work, but I felt being the best in my faculty was something I wanted to work towards. And, of course, that would also mean graduating as the best student in my department. The motivation behind that goal goes back to shortly after secondary school, when my parents enrolled me in a Cambridge A-level programme. sports.title: Rams grind out 26-13 win over Packers on Thanksgiving Eve
sports.description: Nov 25, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love (10) throws a pass during the first quarter against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images INGLEWOOD, Calif. — Blake Corum turned 26 on Wednesday and celebrated with a career-best performance, carrying the ball 32 times for 184 yards and a touchdown as the Los Angeles Rams controlled the clock and the trenches in a 26-13 victory over the Green Bay Packers . It was the NFL’s first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game, and the Rams used it to extend their winning streak to five and improve to 7-4. Corum’s 32 carries were the most by a Rams running back in Sean McVay’s decade in charge. He scored for the seventh straight game, and Kyren Williams added a touchdown and 46 yards on 12 carries as Los Angeles finished with 241 rushing yards. Brandon McManus contributed four field goals. Matthew Stafford needed only 16 completions on 23 attempts for 140 yards (and one interception) as the Rams leaned on the ground game against an injury-thinned receiving corps. The teams were tied 13-13 at halftime. Green Bay had clawed back from an early deficit behind a Christian Watson touchdown catch, but the second half belonged entirely to the Rams. Los Angeles outscored the Packers 13-0 after the break, held Green Bay to just 55 rushing yards, and dominated time of possession (40:40 to 19:20). Jordan Love finished 17-of-29 for 198 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions. The Packers fell to 6-5 after their second straight loss. The night was not without controversy. Rams safety Kamren Kinchens was ejected for a helmet-to-helmet hit on Watson late in the second quarter; Watson was ruled out with a concussion after catching four passes for 65 yards and the score. Micah Parsons, returning from a torn ACL, recorded a sack for Green Bay, but the Packers could not generate consistent offense once the Rams established their rushing rhythm. The result carries clear playoff weight. Both teams entered at 6-4 in a crowded NFC wild-card race; the head-to-head win and the possession edge now give the Rams a clearer path. Los Angeles hosts the Kansas City Chiefs next, while Green Bay travels to face the New Orleans Saints.

sports.title: WNBA’s 2027 Cap Math Leaves Little Room For Error For Dream
sports.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images The WNBA salary cap rules for 2027 create a harsh reality for teams trying to build a winner. The Atlanta Dream faces a math problem that leaves almost no room for maneuvering. According to Sports Illustrated , the league cap can rise by no more than 13% to $7.91 million. This small jump does not help teams that already have limited space. The Dream must sign three new players just to fill their roster. Each of these new signings costs at least $280,800. That adds up fast and eats into the money available for star talent. The Minimum Salary Trap Every team must keep 12 players on the roster during the season. This rule forces franchises to spend money they might prefer to save. Per Sports Illustrated, the lowest full-season minimum salary for a player with no experience is $280,800 in 2027. The Dream already has nine players under contract totaling about $6.18 million. To reach the required 12 players, the team needs to spend an extra $842,400 on new signings. This mandatory spending pushes their total obligations to $7.02 million. The math leaves the team with very little flexibility to sign big free agents. Where the Money Goes The gap between the total cap and what a team can actually spend is now wider than ever. The Atlanta Dream will have to spend $7.02 million just to meet basic roster requirements. This leaves them with about $886,000 to spend freely on top-tier talent. That amount is tiny compared to the cost of a supermax deal. A supermax salary is 20% of the cap for a given year, which would be roughly $1.58 million. Only the current club or, in the event of free agency, the former club can sign an eligible player to a supermax. This restriction makes it hard for other teams to poach stars from the Dream without paying a premium. Spending Limits and Roster Rules A team’s payroll cannot surpass the salary cap at any moment unless it applies a hardship, emergency hardship, pregnancy/childbirth, or season-ending injury exception. For any specific year, the standard maximum salary equals 17% of the salary cap. These tight limits mean teams cannot simply throw money at every problem. They must plan carefully or risk breaking the rules. The Dream’s situation shows how the new rules squeeze out spending power. With only $886,000 left for free spending, the team has very few options to improve the roster beyond the minimums. The Dream, in its present form, must spend $7.02 million, which leaves approximately $886,000 available for unrestricted spending above minimum salaries.

sports.title: Why do the Lions and Cowboys always play on Thanksgiving?
sports.description: Detroit Lions fans dress for Thanksgiving game against the Chicago Bears, Thursday, Nov. 28, 2019 at Ford Field. Detroit Lions fans | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co There are three NFL games today. The Lions host the Bears, the Cowboys host the Eagles, and the Bills host the Chiefs. The teams playing the night game change annually, but you might notice that the Lions always host the first game of the day, and the Cowboys always host the second game. How did that come to be? The Lions played their first Thanksgiving game in 1934. It was their first season in Detroit. They had previously been located in Portsmouth, Ohio, where they were known as the Portsmouth Spartans. A radio executive named George Richards bought the franchise and moved it to Detroit. The Lions were having difficulty gaining any sort of popularity in their new home city. Richards came up with the idea of scheduling their team’s big game against the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving. The Lions were 10-1 at the time, and the Bears were 11-0. This was before the days when the league dictated the schedule to its teams. The teams themselves could schedule the times of their games. Richards used his connections in the radio business to get the game broadcast nationally. Even thought Detroit lost, it was a huge success. The Lions sold the game out, and they have played on Thanksgiving ever since with the exception of World War II years despite some calls for them to lose the game during the dismal Matt Millen Era. Thanksgiving gained a second traditional team in 1951. For the next thirteen years, the Green Bay Packers traveled to Detroit to play the Lions on Thanksgiving. Vince Lombardi ended the arrangement. Lombardi cited the end of an agreement that paid the Packers $10,000 extra for playing the game, the difficulties of playing games on a short week every year, and having to face a rival in front of an electric crowd on the road every season. Of course since the teams are in the same division, the Packers remain a frequent Thanksgiving opponent for Detroit. So how about the Cowboys? In the mid-1960’s the NFL was looking to add a second Thanksgiving game. It was not entirely clear it would work outside Detroit, where Thanksgiving NFL was already a tradition. The Dallas Cowboys were a six year old team with no history of winning. General manager Tex Schramm was a visionary. (He was a driving force behind other innovations like instant replay, the flags on goal posts, the NFL-AFL merger, and too many others to name). He jumped at the opportunity. The Cowboys hosted their first Thanksgiving game in 1966. They kept the game annually until the 1970’s when the league hatched a plan to alternate between the Cowboys and the then St. Louis Cardinals . The Cowboys were to host the second game in even years and the Cardinals in odd years. The Cardinals only hosted two home Thanksgiving games, however, which took place in 1975 and in 1977. You’re authentic, man. And I don’t want you to ever change. Not only in the National Football League but this city, we need more people like Dan Campbell to continue to be a part of this society. As you keep your strive and pursuit for excellence is what’s made this country great, and you represent every element of that. Thank you for being you, and don’t you dare change. After letting Pete Alonso leave for Baltimore last offseason, the Mets decided to replace him with Jorge Polanco, who had never previously played first but profiled as someone who could manage the position and who was coming off his best season by wRC+ (132) and his third-best by fWAR (2.6). sports.description: The story of the Commanders’ season has been playing up to the level of the best teams in the league and playing down to the level of some of the worst ones. Until Week 9, they have struggled to find ways to win close games. For the second week in a row, the Commanders pulled off a game winning drive after the two minute warning. While it may be too early to pronounce a turnaround to the disappointing 2026 season, fans who have kept hope alive for a return to 2024 form would have recognised the calm determination and surgical precision Jayden Daniels showed as he led the team into field goal range with 39 seconds remaining. Over the past few games, the Commanders’ identity has finally started to come into focus. In addition to a magician at QB, Daronte Jones’ aggressive defense is emerging as a strength. The Bengals rank 4 th in total points. Prior to facing the Commanders, they were averaging 30.9 point per game. The Commanders are one of only three teams to hold them to under 27 points, along with the Jaguars and Texans. That level of defense, and a quarterback who is up to any challenge, can allow them to compete with the best teams in football, if they can just stay out of their own way. Drew Stevens’ 26 yard field goal with time expiring sealed the Commanders’ first back-to-back win since the divisional round of the 2024 playoffs. They need to keep stacking the wins to catch up with the division-leading Giants and keep their playoff-hopes alive. Fortunately, they only need to tie the Giants’ win total to win the division, thanks to the Week 10 win giving them the advantage of the head-to-head tiebreaker. The Commanders only play two opponents with winning records in seven remaining games, while the Giants have yet to run the gauntlet of the 49ers, Seahawks and Lions. Hopefully the Cowboys stay out of the mix. But the Commanders may have the opportunity to settle the matter if Jerry’s boys make it close by the Week 18 rematch. There is still a lot of football left to play. Against the 7-2 Bengals, the Commanders did what they needed to do to keep their season alive. technology.title: Rackspace pulls plug on Spot cloud service after security breach
technology.description: Rackspace is shutting down its low-cost Spot cloud service after a security breach, giving customers two weeks' notice to move their workloads and retrieve their data. In a notice posted on Tuesday , the cloud computing biz said its Rackspace Spot service will cease operations at 1700 Central Time (2300 UTC) on December 8. Any workloads still running at that point will be terminated, and customers will no longer be able to access their data. "Following the recent security incident affecting Rackspace Spot, Rackspace has made the decision to wind down the service," the company said. "Spot customers are being notified with the wind-down timeline, instructions for retrieving their data and steps to secure their environments." Customers will have to contend with the fallout from the breach while simultaneously trying to get their applications and data off the platform. According to a customer notification seen by The Register , the attackers used leaked credentials to access parts of Rackspace Spot over a period of almost 22 hours on November 17. Rackspace only learned of the intrusion the following day, after a customer raised the alarm. The intruders impersonated legitimate users, created pods in customer Kubernetes clusters, gained access to stored credentials known as Kubernetes Secrets, and listed nodes and storage volumes. "With that access, they could have read any Secret in an affected user's clusters, and any Spot API token or refresh token that user held," Rackspace told customers. Rackspace has since revoked the affected tokens and sessions, removed the pods planted by the intruders, and changed the affected platform and storage keys. Customers must also reissue API tokens, download new Kubernetes configuration files, and rotate credentials stored in their clusters, including database passwords and third-party API keys. Sirish Raghuram, co-founder and chief growth officer of Platform9, which co-developed Spot with Rackspace, shed some light on the root cause in a November 20 GitHub post. "An observability system was breached using a compromised credential," Raghuram wrote. "This was obviously a critical error on our part and we are very sorry we let this happen." Raghuram said the incident necessitated significant changes to the underlying infrastructure clusters, prolonging the outage. Spot's selling point was cheap compute. The service operated an auction-based pricing model, allowing customers to bid for cloud infrastructure at a fraction of the cost of conventional on-demand instances. Rackspace advertised savings of up to 90 percent for customers willing to tolerate interruptions to their workloads. A permanent interruption probably wasn't what they had in mind. Rackspace hasn't explained why it chose closure over recovery, revealed how many customers were affected, or said whether it will offer migration extensions. It did not respond to The Register's questions. ®

technology.title: Wyoming uranium operation shuts down after cyberattack
technology.description: Peninsula Energy has temporarily shut down its Wyoming uranium operation after a "cybersecurity incident" affected plant and wellfield control systems. The Australian uranium producer said on Wednesday that it had activated its response procedures and brought in outside specialists following the attack on its US subsidiary, Strata Energy, which operates the Lance uranium project. Peninsula Energy said it believes the attack is "confined to the plant and wellfield operating and control systems," and that back-office functions, such as payroll and other corporate systems, in both the US and Australia, remain unaffected. "The company's immediate priorities have been to protect the safety of its employees, secure its operating systems, and work towards the restoration of operations in a safe and controlled manner," it said in an update to the Australian Securities Exchange. The notification [PDF] went on to say that Peninsula Energy's investigations into the attack, including whether any data was compromised, remain ongoing. Peninsula has not given a restart date and says it cannot yet assess the impact on its 2027 production guidance. Operations will remain suspended until recovery and safety checks are complete. "Peninsula will provide further updates to the market as material information becomes available," it said. The disclosure of additional information came two days after Peninsula secured a short trading halt, which referenced a cybersecurity incident at its Wyoming site. The November 23 filing [PDF] dated the incident to Friday evening in Western Australia. Wednesday's update clarified that Strata detected it on the morning of November 20, local US time. Peninsula subsequently requested a voluntary suspension of trading until the earlier of November 30 or an announcement on restarting operations and any resulting change to production guidance. Peninsula's Lance project is a uranium mining operation, extracting the element from underground deposits and turning it into uranium concentrate, aka yellowcake or U₃O₈. Uranium concentrate is feedstock for nuclear fuel production, typically undergoing conversion, enrichment, and fabrication into uranium dioxide pellets before use in reactors. The Lance central processing plant was constructed to produce a maximum of 2.0 million pounds (Mlb) of U₃O₈ annually, and is licensed for 3.0 Mlb. Peninsula previously forecast production of 500,000 to 600,000 pounds in 2027, having withdrawn its 2026 guidance earlier this year following operational problems at Lance. It now says it will reassess the 2027 outlook once operations resume. ®

technology.title: Company was religious about backups but sinned by leaving them exposed
technology.description: Welcome, once again, to PWNED, where we’re thankful every time someone leaves a password sticky note on a monitor or fails to delete a terminated employee’s admin account. But neither of those common occurrences is what we’ll be talking about today. Instead, our subject broke the number-one rule of backups: you gotta keep ’em separated. Our story comes courtesy of Da Li, who serves as global alliance manager at Info2Soft , a company that provides data protection and recovery software. At one point, a partner called him into a case where a Chinese vehicle parts manufacturer fell victim to a ransomware gang. Unfortunately, its backup was compromised too. The manufacturer had religiously backed up its manufacturing execution system (MES) and SAP orders, inventory, and finance systems every night. There was even a green dashboard that showed the backup process had succeeded, and someone checked that every morning. However, one Friday evening, crims broke into the network and found out that the backup server was joined to the same Windows domain as the rest of the network. The hackers found a plaintext password for the backup service account in a maintenance script on a file share and discovered that someone had used the very same password for a domain admin account. So the first thing the crooks did was delete every restore point on that backup server. Then they started encrypting the production servers to ransom them. “Every backup job had succeeded for three years,” Li said. “The failure was that the thing meant to save them could be reached with the same keys as the thing being attacked.” The results were devastating. With the MES and SAP data both gone, the plant couldn't schedule production, ship parts, or track them. By the time Li was called in, the plant had already resolved its ransomware situation. We don’t know whether it paid or not. The manufacturer did ask Li and his company to make sure that this couldn’t happen again. Li’s fix was not radical, but it was instructive. He made sure that the company now keeps its backup system outside the production domain, uses unique credentials, and requires MFA to reduce the risk of unauthorized access even if a password is compromised. He also made sure that the company keeps at least one offline backup and runs a test restore quarterly to ensure it’s prepared for emergencies.®

technology.title: Microsoft hotpatches hotpatch that could crash Windows Server 2025
technology.description: Microsoft has released an out-of-band hotpatch to fix a bug in November's Windows Server 2025 security update that could crash some servers when an IPv6 route expires. The patch for the patch, KB5138318 , addresses crashes on systems with Router Advertisement (RA) enabled that receive time-bound IPv6 routes. When a route timer expires, affected servers can halt with error 0x139 (KERNEL_SECURITY_CHECK_FAILURE). Issued on November 25, the corrective update takes effect without requiring a restart, according to Microsoft. KERNEL_SECURITY_CHECK_FAILURE means the kernel has detected corruption of a critical data structure and stopped the system. Microsoft has identified route-timer expiry as the trigger but hasn't explained the underlying coding fault. Good to see the operating system being protected against the impact of the corruption. Less good for administrators wondering why their servers have suddenly misbehaved. Lansweeper puts Windows Server 2025 at 7 percent of the servers it monitors, compared with 32 percent for Server 2022 and 33 percent for Server 2019. Only systems with the affected hotpatch and networking configuration are implicated. Microsoft's Windows Server updates have not gone well over the last few months, with out-of-band updates issued in September, October, and November. An out-of-band update to deal with a problem introduced in a hotpatch (in this case, KB5131077 ) therefore carries with it a certain sense of inevitability. Hotpatches are a way of getting OS security updates on a Windows Server without requiring a restart and so are, in theory, a boon for administrators keen on maximizing uptime. According to Microsoft, in addition to faster installations and better protection, there is "lower workload impact with less need to restart your machine." Avoiding a planned restart is less of a selling point when the alternative is an unplanned crash. ®

technology.title: Draining peatlands is responsible for a few percent of our global warming
technology.description: Much of the focus for human-caused climate change is on fossil fuels, which are creating most of our problems. But land use change is also a large component of the story, accounting for about one-third of total historical CO 2 emissions. Deforestation plays a major role here, but practices like draining wetlands also factor in. Exactly how much of our history of eliminating wetlands has contributed to warming is challenging to figure out. But thanks to new sources of data that measure emissions from today’s surviving wetlands, it’s possible to put a better number on it. A new study led by Jevan Yu at MIT focuses on peatlands—environments like bogs and fens where organic matter accumulates into thick layers of material. Some 600 billion tons of carbon are held in these vast stores of peat, which is more than you can find in all the world’s living vegetation, the researchers note. Because these areas are permanently inundated, any oxygen in the water is quickly used up, leaving the job of decaying all that organic matter to anaerobic bacteria that work much more slowly and don't digest everything. So instead of seeing organic carbon turning into the CO 2 gas released by aerobic bacteria, in peatlands, a subset of it gradually turns into methane gas. Methane is an even more potent greenhouse gas than CO 2 itself and ultimately gets oxidized into CO 2 . That means there’s a little trade-off from peatlands—most of the carbon they have is kept out of the atmosphere, but the carbon that does escape does so as methane. Read full article Comments
